title: HUANUO Dual Monitor Stand, Fully Adjustable Monitor Desk Mount for 13–32″ Computer Screens, Full Motion VESA 75x75/100x100 with C-Clamp & Grommet Base, Each Arm Holds 4.4 to 19.8 lbs -Grey
reviews: Mount is very sturdy and very well made. Very easy to mount to the desk, I had to use the screw mount rather than the clamp mount, and it's solid as a rock. I have two 27" curved monitors attached to this mount and once they were set, and I made a couple of adjustments at the hinges, the monitors stayed exactly how I positioned them. No bobbing up or down or twisting off the vertical plane. Very stable and switching to this mount, from the stands that came with the monitors has freed up a tremendous amount of desk space. This mount is a little more expensive than some of the other mounts but it's well worth the cost! I highly recommend it.

I have several monitor mounted on desk-mounted arm and these are great. They save desk space and make it easy to adjust the workspace for different tasks. I have had this particular dual arm for a few months and they have performed well. They are easy to adjust and after a little initial tweaking (if needed), you can easily pivot, swivel and rotate your monitor into the exact position you prefer. I have 27" monitors on the arms and nothing has sagged or tilted in an undesired way. I had no missing parts, assembly was easy and it quickly secured to the desk. I haven't had a monitor arm fail yet, and expect the same from these. I will update if their durability isn't up to expectations.

Updating our workspace at the office with dual monitor setups and this model had good reviews, so I thought I'd try it out. I have now purchased 7 of these and will keep buying them as the update expands. They are relatively inexpensive, very heavy duty, offer great flexibility for installation, as well as monitor placement once installed, and come with enough extra hardware to accommodate many different monitor sizes. I would highly recommend!

I'm pretty impressed with this dual monitor arm, and see why it's (currently) amazons "recommended". Installation is straightforward and when doing the C-clamp style mounting, the instructions are completely unnecessary. The arms are very sturdy, and can be locked into position once the desired location is set. It holds my Acer 32" monitor without breaking a sweat (though it's a very light screen, to be fair. Lighter than alot of 27" ones i've owned) though it struggles a bit with my featherlight 15" second screen. This isn't a downside to the stand, as it explicitly gives a weight rating it needs to work with, and the small screen i use is FAR below the minimum weight. Becuase of this, with the arm tension loosened all the way, I'm just BARELY able to mount that screen as low as possible. If i give it any upwards force, or try to raise it even a centimeter, the springs will launch the arm (and monitor) all the way up, which jars the entire desk. So, just something to be aware of. Again, this is MY problem, not the fault of the stand, as i'm not using it in it's intended fashion. I only really have 2 complaints, and theyre things ive noticed on the 3 seperate sets of these i've bought over the last 6 months....the tension bolts are INCREDIBLY tight and can be very difficult to adjust for someone who might not have the most wrist/grip strength. And finally, they include 2 sizes of screws. The longer ones are M4x30 screws, to be used in conjunction with some rubber/plastic spacers for curved monitors. So far, on every monitor I have paired with these (with the exception of one Dell 27" with a dummy thicc plastic back shroud) the M4x30 screws have bottomed out on EVERY other monitor, far before they were actually tight, resulting in a loose, wobbly screen. So, maybe plan on making a potential run to the hardware store for some M4x25's to use instead. Those two reasons are why I deducted a star. Aside from that, these are exactly what I needed and I have zero additional complaints. I would highly recommend, and, as I've already bought multiple of these, I think thats a testimony in itself.

These are some of the best monitor stands out there I've used. The floating arms won't quite be as flexible as you'd like, but they're WAY easier to use than the standard straight pole, straight arm stands. You can even rotate your monitors straight up while plugged in to check which ports you're using if they're on the bottom of the monitor. They hold the weight of two 27" monitors flawlessly, I've had older and heavier 4k monitors on these arms and they still supported them easily. Super easy to install, it just pinch/vice grips your desk with a really sturdy base, just buy these already.
Great product. Rather easy to assemble and install. Works great for my 2 23” monitors. Clears up desk space and holds the monitors up at a better height for me.

I wasn’t expecting to like this as much as I do, but this monitor stand completely upgraded my desk setup. Setup was extremely fast and easy, and once it’s on the desk, it feels very sturdy and secure. No wobbling, even when adjusting the monitors. It supports both of my screens easily and holds position well thanks to the spring arms. The biggest win for me is the range of motion—you can adjust height, tilt, swivel, and even rotate the screens, which makes it easy to find a comfortable setup whether you’re working or gaming. It also cleared up a ton of desk space, which I didn’t realize I needed until I had it. A couple small things to note: • It does take a bit of effort to get the tension adjusted perfectly at first • You’ll want a solid desk since the clamp is strong (which is a good thing, just something to be aware of) •. It can look a bit bulky if you have a smaller width desk. I recommend a wider desk, so the monitors aren’t too close to your face. Overall, this is one of those upgrades that actually makes a difference day-to-day. If you’re using two monitors and want a cleaner, more ergonomic setup without spending a ton, this is definitely worth it.
Perhaps a little premature for only using it for 15 mins, but this was an easy assembly, feels very solid, and the price was right. I'll report back after 20 mins.
